facts.big: the café that opened last week
facts.label: That em orações relativas
facts.sub: Use that depois de um lugar ou coisa para dizer qual: the café that opened, the latte that I love. O verbo vem logo depois, sem it.

facts.label: Que, o qual
facts.sub: Use that depois de um lugar ou coisa: the café that opened last week. O verbo vem logo depois de that. Não repita it depois dele.

facts.label: that + sujeito + verbo
facts.sub: Também podemos ter that + sujeito: the pastries that they bake. Aqui that é o objeto. Nessa estrutura, o that pode sumir: the pastries they bake.

compare.ask: It is the café that opened last week.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “o café que abriu” e o “que” serve para tudo.
compare.tip: Diga: “It is the café that opened last week.”
compare.us: Em inglês, para lugares e coisas use that: the café that opened. O verbo vem logo depois, sem it.

paragraphs: It is a rainy Tuesday morning in Portland. A new café opened on the corner last week. Finn sees a long line outside the door. His friend Luisa is walking by. She already knows the place well. Finn wants to hear all about it.

“Luisa, have you tried the café that opened last week?” says Finn. “Yes! It is the place that has the best oat milk coffee.” says Luisa. “I heard it is a café that serves fresh pastries too.” says Finn.
